intro.caption: Side B. Your first performance. … Rule one: repeat only the lines I give you. Rule two: when I say pause, pause. Rule three: when something goes wrong, wind me back ten seconds and listen again — this course anticipates everything. Even you. … Seat your subject across from you, phone between you, face up. Pause here. Play when you're both ready.

ind1.caption: 「TO YOUR SUBJECT」 Close your eyes. You're in school again — ten, maybe twelve. Last period. A pencil in your hand, and without deciding to, you're doodling the same small doodle you always drew. Five, ten seconds of pencil. Not a smiley face. Not a mountain. Not a bicycle. No circles or triangles. A real thing anybody would recognize. See it on the page. Don't say it. Pause — play when they nod.

ind2.caption: 「TO YOUR SUBJECT」 Put the real thing in the room — real size, right there between you. Now think of it as a WORD (a smiley face would be the word SMILEY). Walk its letters one at a time… again, slower… good. 「TO YOU」 Ask: “Do you have it?” A nod is enough. Pause — play when they nod.

preflight.caption: From here, you say only Gerald's words. Deep breath. Straight back. Dead eyes. Here we go.

20.caption: First impression. Say it calm, like you're reading a menu: “I can feel a letter in your word. An A. There's an A… correct?” Then pause.

21.caption: Of course there's an A. There always is, with Gerald. Now say: “I see a T as well… yes?” Pause.

22.caption: Two for two. Don't get cocky. Softer this time: “Is that… an R?” Pause.

23.caption: Look at you. Almost dangerous. Last letter — barely believe it: “Now I'm not sure about this one… an S?” Pause.

24.caption: [click] You rewound me — so they said no. Fine. FINE. Shoulders down; doubt has a smell. Say: “No… no, it's leaning — it's an S. There IS an S.” Pause.

25m.caption: [click] No T. Interesting — steady. Say it as a FACT, not a question: “This thing you drew — it is NOT a living thing.” If they agree: play. If they argue: you know the rule.

25.caption: Agreed — not alive. See how easy? Say: “Hold out your hand. Imagine it there. Could you HOLD it in one hand?” Pause.

26.caption: [click] No R. They're fine — YOU are 'adequate'. New angle: “Leave the letters. Let me touch the thing itself. Is it ALIVE?” Pause.

27.caption: There it is — we're back. Now the body does the work. Say: “Reach out in your mind. Can you TOUCH it?” Pause.

28.caption: [click] No A. No S. Whatever you're doing with your face — stop. Letters are not your instrument; we go to RAW IMPRESSIONS. Say: “Forget letters. Forget words. I'm getting something warmer. Is it ALIVE?” Pause.

29.caption: I thought so — I felt it in the palm too. Say: “Squeeze it. Is it HARD?” Pause.

30.caption: [click] Too big for a hand — exactly where Gerald wants us. Say: “It's bigger than both of us. Tell me — do you OWN one?” Pause.

31.caption: Alive — Gerald can hear it moving. Say: “Stand next to it in your mind. Is it SMALLER than you?” Pause.

32.caption: [click] Not alive — but it relates to life, tell them: “It relates to life… it's part of a day.” Then: “Do you have one at HOME?” Pause.

33.caption: Touchable — reach further. Say: “I'm touching it with you… wait. I sense… LIFE. Is it alive?” Pause.

34.caption: Alive! The impressions like you better than the letters did. Say: “Stand next to it. Is it BIGGER than you?” Pause.

35.caption: [click] Not alive. Close now — Gerald can feel edges. Say: “Reach for it. Can you TOUCH it?” Pause.

36.caption: Wet? WET. Say: “Scales. A little bubble over its head.” … “You drew a FISH.” Now turn the screen around.

37.caption: [click] Say exactly: “It's not alive — but it is FULL of life. It's where the life lives.” Watch their face. Then: “Square walls. Triangle roof. Smoke from the chimney. You drew a HOUSE.” Turn the screen around.

38.caption: [click] Untouchable — and everything untouchable is magnificent. Say: “Of course you can't touch it. It's ninety-three million miles away — you drew it in the corner of the page with little lines coming off it. You drew the SUN.” Turn the screen around.

39.caption: Bigger, alive, older than everyone here. Say: “Roots down. Branches up. The leaves were one big cloud, weren't they. You drew a TREE.” Turn the screen around.

40.caption: [click] Smaller. Delicate. Say: “A stem. Petals in a ring. You pressed harder on the middle. You drew a FLOWER.” Turn the screen around.

41.caption: Touchable — and someone in this story is holding its cousin. Say: “Long. Thin. A point at one end. You drew the thing you were drawing WITH. You drew a PENCIL.” Turn the screen around.

42.caption: [click] Untouchable, far away, cold silver. Say: “You drew it as a crescent — a little banana in the sky — with stars around it. You drew the MOON.” Turn the screen around.

43.caption: Hard — and cold, which is the giveaway. Say: “A stem. A bowl. A toast at the end of a long week. You drew a GLASS.” Turn the screen around.

44.caption: [click] Soft skin, full of air. Say: “It wants to be thrown. It spends its whole life leaving. You drew a BALL.” Turn the screen around.

45.caption: They own one — Gerald has, in a manner of speaking, sat in it. Say: “Four wheels. Windows. Parked outside a childhood house. You drew a CAR.” Turn the screen around.

46.caption: [click] Nobody owns one — it belongs to the sky. Say: “You drew it with little windows down the side, didn't you. You drew a PLANE.” Turn the screen around.

47.caption: Small, warm, and completely indifferent to us both. Say: “Whiskers. Pointed ears. It's ignoring you right now. You drew a CAT.” Turn the screen around.

48.caption: [click] Not smaller — exactly your size. It always was. Say: “A round head. Stick arms straight out. A self-portrait, age ten. You drew a STICKMAN — you drew YOU.” Turn the screen around.

rman.caption: [click] They ARGUED? Good — arguing means a pulse. Say: “You drew a person. Round head, stick arms straight out. That's YOU, isn't it.” Turn the screen around.

49.caption: At home — you've eaten off yours tonight. Say: “Four legs. A flat top. The whole family around it. You drew a TABLE.” Turn the screen around.

50.caption: [click] Not at home — it lives on the water. Say: “A little hull. A sail. You always drew the waves as tiny W's, didn't you. You drew a BOAT.” Turn the screen around.

51.caption: [click] No S… after A, T, R… oh. OH. Stand up straighter. Say: “It's not letters anymore — I can FEEL this one. It's beating. You drew a HEART.” Turn the screen around.

52.caption: Four letters, four hits — this is what Side A was FOR. Slowly: “You were ten years old, bored out of your mind… and you reached for the sky. You drew a STAR.” Turn the screen around.

finale.caption: Let them have their moment. Don't explain anything — not that you could. You were adequate: Gerald's highest grade. The rest of this side is licensing information. Press ■ to rewind for your next subject.
